title: Prime-field identification of one finite trivial quotient
statement: Let K, Ks and Omega be fields in universe u, with compatible embeddings K -> Ks -> Omega [def-pd-separable-closure], and Omega algebraically closed. Let G=Gal(Ks/K) with the Krull topology, let H be an open subgroup of G, and set L=(Ks)^H. Assume Ks is a separable closure of K. A fixed-field comparison C consists of an equivalence E from abelian etale sheaves on Spec L [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] to discrete continuous integer H-modules [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], a natural additive isomorphism j from the underlying group of E(F) to the geometric stalk F_p at the point p:Spec Omega -> Spec L induced by L -> Ks -> Omega [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and the following action compatibility. For every F, g in H, K-automorphism tau of Omega extending g on Ks, etale L-scheme X, pointed lifts x,x' of p with x'=Spec(tau) followed by x, and section z of F on X, j_F(g*j_F^{-1}(germ_x(z)))=germ_x'(z). Let T be a scheme in universe u and e:Spec L ~= T an isomorphism. For a specified discrete H-module V define P_C(V)=(e.inv)^*(E.inverse(V)) using inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let R be a discrete continuous integer G-representation with underlying abelian group R.V in universe u+1. Restrict it to H with the same action. For an H-invariant additive subgroup B of R.V, write V_B for its canonical integer submodule with this restricted action; its underlying elements are exactly x in B. For additive subgroups A,B of R.V put N=A.toIntSubmodule.comap(B.toIntSubmodule.subtype). Let Q_{A,B} be the discrete H-module with underlying group B.toIntSubmodule/N and trivial H-action. Assume R.V is finite. Let ell be prime and assume ell*x belongs to A for every x in B. No inclusion A<=B is required: N is their relative intersection in B. Then there exists a natural number d such that P_C(Q_{A,B}) is isomorphic to the iterated binary biproduct defined by Z(0)=0 and Z(d+1)=Z(d) biproduct T.constantZMod(ell) [def-sc-constant-sheaves].

proof.text: Put Q = B.toIntSubmodule / primaryRelativeSubmodule. Its underlying type is finite: inclusion of B into the finite ambient group is injective, and the quotient map is surjective. Quotient induction and mk_smul show that ell kills Q. Give Q its ZMod ell module structure and restrict scalars from ULift (ZMod ell). Choose the vector-space basis; its index injects into the finite group Q, hence is finite. Reindex by Fin d and apply the coordinate equivalence to obtain Q additively isomorphic to Fin d -> ULift (ZMod ell).

For any abelian group V, let F be its constant sheaf on Spec L and a the canonical map from global constant sections to its geometric stalk at t. The constant geometric stalk theorem makes a an isomorphism. Compose it with the inverse of the given fiber comparison to obtain an additive isomorphism b: V -> C(F). For g in H, extend g to tau on Omega. Each y in L is fixed by g, so the extension identity shows tau fixes the image of L and Spec(tau) followed by t equals t. Apply the comparison action formula at the identity etale neighbourhood with both lifts equal to t and the global constant section of v. Cancel the fiber isomorphism to prove g*b(v)=b(v). The resulting integer-linear equivariant isomorphism is an isomorphism of discrete representations. Apply C.inverse and its unit to identify the inverse of the trivial representation with F; pull back across e.inv using upperStarConstantSheafIso.

Prove by induction on d that the constant sheaf of Fin d -> ULift (ZMod ell) is the displayed Nat.rec biproduct. For d=0 its coefficient group is subsingleton and the additive constant-sheaf functor sends it to a zero object. For d+1 use Fin.snocEquiv and product commutation to split off one coefficient. The additive-group product is the binary biproduct; the constant-sheaf functor preserves binary biproducts because it preserves coproducts and is additive. Compose with the induction isomorphism.

Compose the trivial-representation/constant-sheaf isomorphism for Q, the constant-sheaf image of its coordinate additive equivalence, and the finite-biproduct induction. The result is the required witness d and isomorphism. A=B and B=0 give the zero quotient; no inclusion A<=B is used.

theorem primaryTrivialQuotient_constant
    (K Ks Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field Ks] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K Ks] [IsSepClosure K Ks] [Algebra Ks Ω] [Algebra K Ω]
    [IsScalarTower K Ks Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (H : OpenSubgroup (Gal(Ks/K))) (C : PrimaryFixedFieldEquivalence K Ks H)
    (hC : PrimaryFixedFieldComparison K Ks H Ω C)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (e : Spec (.of (IntermediateField.fixedField H.toSubgroup)) ≅ T)
    (R : Rep.DiscreteContinuousRep.{0, u, u + 1} ℤ (Gal(Ks/K))) [Finite R.obj.V]
    (A B : AddSubgroup R.obj.V) (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    (hkill : ∀ x : R.obj.V, x ∈ B → ℓ • x ∈ A) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, Nonempty
      (primaryAssociatedSheaf K Ks H Ω C T e (primaryTrivialQuotient K Ks H R A B) ≅
        Nat.rec (0 : _) (fun _ V ↦ V ⊞ T.constantZMod ℓ) d)
